evals.name: offline-sync-electron
evals.prompt: I want to add a proper offline mode to my Electron notes app (React + SQLite through better-sqlite3, syncs to a Rails backend). Conflict resolution, a sync queue, the lot. Create a very detailed plan with distinct phases for this task - this plan should be ready for orcestrator and sub-agents execution, meaning an orchestrator fires sub-agent to execute a phase, one at a time. This is needed so that a main plan execution session won't blow up on context tokens size
evals.expected_output: A phased plan document, explicitly orchestrator-ready
assertions: Contains a phase map table listing every phase with a named test or verification scenario
States explicitly that the orchestrator does not read source files, only the plan, the handoff and the reports
Contains a reusable sub-agent prompt template with fill-in placeholders, not just prose about firing agents
Names a specific handoff log file path and says what each phase appends to it
The first phase measures unknowns or proves the risky mechanism, instead of building a user-facing feature
Every phase section has a Reads list naming specific files to open
Every phase has a Done-when tied to a runnable command or named test, with at least one numeric or countable assertion
Tells sub-agents to stop and report rather than widen scope when a check keeps failing
Tells the orchestrator to run one sub-agent at a time and keep every phase green before starting the next
The cross-cutting constraints appear both at the top of the plan and inside the sub-agent prompt template
The last phase writes the docs through a sub-agent, and a separate fresh agent checks them against the handoff log and the code before the plan is closed
The sub-agent prompt says the reply only summarizes the handoff entry, with nothing in the reply that is not in the log
Conflict resolution is specified concretely, naming a strategy and its tie-breakers, not left as 'handle conflicts'
